author: fwyzard
body:
### 2.2.0 The New Warp Order

This release brings new memory ordering support, masked warp operations, and further improvements to alpaka's type-safe interface. `alpaka::mem_fence()` now supports explicit memory orderings, while warp functions gain mask support through the new `alpaka::warp::Mask` type. Warp functionality is also implemented for the SYCL backend, with `activemask` support added for HIP. Other highlights include support for grid-wide kernel synchronisation and a new interface for external memory allocators.

The public interface is further strengthened with C++ concepts for `Device`, `Queue`, and `Platform`, alongside the existing `View` concept. Buffer allocation can now deduce the index type, views can be created from queues, and memory operations support buffers and views with different index types. Runtime extent checks replace the previous compile-time index-type checks.

Support is extended to recent compiler and accelerator ecosystems, including CUDA 13.4, ROCm 10.0, oneAPI 2026.1, and Clang 23. New AMD RDNA 4, RDNA 5, and CDNA 4 GPU targets are supported, together with updated SYCL GPU targets.

The release also contains numerous improvements to diagnostics, CMake integration, documentation, CI, tests, and compatibility with newer compilers and SDKs, as well as fixes across the CUDA, HIP, SYCL, and CPU backends.

The full list of changes is available in the [ChangeLog](https://github.com/alpaka-group/alpaka/blob/2.2.0/CHANGELOG.md).
